description: The main objective of the course is to enable the students to develop a complete web application that includes frontend, backend and data-exchange technologies.

syllabus.title: Planning Your Work
syllabus.body: Rise of the web, mobile web, applications vs. web sites, identifying and tracking requirements, Scrum, Kanban, continuous improvement, prioritization & estimation, managing bugs, continuous delivery.

syllabus.title: Designing Systems
syllabus.body: System architectures, identifying concepts and user interactions, handling commonalities, working with legacy and external dependencies, component interactions, cross-functional requirements, caching, designing for failure, designing modules, refactoring.

syllabus.title: Front End
syllabus.body: HTML: from server to browser, styling, components, responsive design, progressive enhancement, SEO, build tools, test-driven development. JavaScript: in the browser, offline-first development, DOM, server-side JavaScript, JavaScript modules and structuring.

syllabus.title: Back-End Development and Storing Data
syllabus.body: Server-side programming languages (e.g., Node.js, Python, Ruby), APIs, designing and securing a REST API, storing data, types of databases, SQL vs. NoSQL, accessing and managing data, protecting your data.

outcomes: Learn about the most recent web development technologies.
Understand the basics of HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap to structure and style web pages.
Acquire awareness about the front end and back-end tools.
textbooks: Chris Northwood, The Full Stack Developer: Your Essential Guide to the Everyday Skills Expected of a Modern Full Stack Web Developer, Apress, 2018.
referenceBooks: Jon Duckett, Web Design with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and JQuery Set, Wiley, 2014.
Nicholas C. Zakas, Professional JavaScript for Web Developers, Wiley, 2012.
